Claude-3.desc: createKeyEchoCatalogue's generic signature (Catalogue extends Record<string,unknown> -> Catalogue) is asserted sound but not demonstrated; JSON-imported catalogue leaf strings may type as string literals rather than widened string, which could make the recursive walker's string-typed replacement value unassignable back into Catalogue without a cast this repo's conventions forbid. Codex-1.desc: Literal string 'test' is not valid BCP-47 syntax - Intl.getCanonicalLocales('test') and new Intl.DateTimeFormat('test') both throw RangeError (verified by direct node execution, not from training), and would fail axe-core's html-lang-valid rule (accessibility.spec.ts, right-to-left.spec.ts). Locale.Test's underlying value must be a syntactically valid BCP-47 tag. Verified 'qtz' (ISO 639-2 private-use range qaa-qtz, single-segment, exactly what pseudo-localization tooling conventionally uses) canonicalizes cleanly with no exceptions and needs no change to the subtag-splitting detection design.
Codex-1.disposition: resolved: locale value changed to 'zxx' (IANA-registered ISO 639-2, meaning 'no linguistic content') after 'pseudo' (round-1 fix) was found by Codex's own executed axe-core 4.13.0 probe to fail html-lang-valid despite passing Intl's grammar-only check. 'zxx' verified against both Intl.getCanonicalLocales/DateTimeFormat AND a real axe-core run - confirmed both by Codex's own round-2 statement and by this session's independent re-execution against the repo's installed axe-core

Codex-2.desc: createKeyEchoCatalogue's contract never requires non-mutation of the source catalogue object; an in-place recursive walker would mutate the cached JSON module import, so a later English registration in the same process could receive key-echoed values instead of real English, contradicting invariant 10. Generator must build a new object tree and never mutate its input; needs a test asserting the source catalogue is unchanged after generation and after a test-then-English registration sequence.
Codex-2.disposition: resolved: invariant 6 now requires non-mutation explicitly with a corresponding test requirement; confirmed by Codex round-2 pass

Codex-3.desc: Invariant 16 ('both loadTranslations.test.ts need no change') contradicts the Testing and validation section (which requires adding Locale.Test cases to the same files per invariants 9-10). Reword invariant 16: the existing explicit language:'en' case needs no change, but new test cases are ADDED to the same files for the Locale.Test branch.
Codex-3.disposition: resolved: invariant 16 reworded to state both files gain a new test case while the existing case is unchanged, matching the testing plan; confirmed by Codex round-2 pass

Codex-4.desc: Invariant 20's claim that the generator lands in each route's lazy chunk (not the entry) is an unverified assumption about Vite/Rollup's chunking algorithm - a module statically imported by two independent lazy route graphs could get hoisted into a shared chunk outside any budget .size-limit.json currently names. retro.outcome: 1) Locale tag validity has two independent layers - Intl.getCanonicalLocales checks BCP-47 grammar only, axe-core's html-lang-valid checks IANA registry membership. 'pseudo' passed the first and failed the second; only caught because Codex actually EXECUTED axe-core against it rather than reasoning from training. My own first G1 validator pass claimed 'should not throw... FROM TRAINING, not executed' and was simply wrong - reinforces codex-contract.md's warning that a well-formed verdict from training isn't proof, but the sharper lesson is: when two DIFFERENT validation mechanisms exist for the same value, passing one says nothing about the other - always identify and check every relevant validator, not just the first one that comes to mind. 2) npm run preview serves dist/ as-is and does NOT rebuild - a stale dist/ (built hours before this session, unrelated to any of today's code) produced a full false-negative e2e run (12/12 failed) before I realized the build was stale, not the wiring. Worth a VERIFICATION.md callout for any repo where preview/e2e depends on a pre-built dist/. 3) Platform-layer boundary rules (platform cannot import app/feature, even in TEST files) apply beyond production code - a spec's testing plan assumed real-catalogue imports in a platform-layer unit test without checking this, caught only during implementation (step 3), not by either G1 review round. Worth a loop-spec-validator prompt addition: explicitly check that every planned test file's imports respect the architecture's layer boundaries, not just production code's. 4) Process error on my part: generated G4's fix-diff evidence via 'git diff main...HEAD' BEFORE committing the fix, so the diff silently showed only pre-fix state - caught by the fresh reviewer reading the actual on-disk files instead of trusting the diff artifact. Lesson: always commit before generating diff-based evidence, or diff against the working tree explicitly, never assume a diff-since-base captures uncommitted work.
